utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have two points to inform the Trial Chamber. First of all, regarding the schedule of the current witness, Mr. Hutsch will certainly be here through the end of our session on Thursday, so there is no worry about finishing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If we take that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we take that long, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Second point is that Your Honours may recall that yesterday my colleague, Mr. Mettraux, showed Mr. Hutsch a newspaper article that referred to a letter from the Prosecutor, Carla Del Ponte. During the breaks yesterday, I searched for such a letter, first in the correspondence of Madam Del Ponte, then in the Deputy Prosecutor, and then in the office of the Chief of Prosecutions. During one of the breaks, I found a letter from the Chief of Prosecutions to the attorney for Mr. Hutsch, as well as a letter from the attorney, a prior letter from the attorney, which had precipitated this letter in response from the Chief of Prosecutions. The letter from the Chief of Prosecutions was sent to Mr. Hutsch' lawyer, I believe, on the 15th of September, 2005. And yesterday afternoon, at about 6.00, I provided copies of both letters to -- to counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are we ready for the witness then?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can I remind you of the affirmation which applies still.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And Mr. Mettraux was in the course of his questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall last night, when we parted, we were discussing a request by the Defence to obtain the -- a set of notes, reporter's note, that covered the date 5 to 24 of August 2001. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to clarify a matter, which to me was very clear on the record. And is it correct that, in response to the question that I put to you, you indicated that those notes, which, in particular the notes of the 10th and 11th of August of 2001, contain material which related both to the events, which you say you witnessed in or around Ljuboten, and information pertaining to other events, and it is based on that fact that you declined to provide the notes to the Defence? Was that the correct understanding that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was the correct understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that's not what you told the Prosecutor when they asked you for those letters?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall what you told the Office of the Prosecutor when Mr. Kuehnel contacted you asking for those letters -- I'm sorry, for those records, reports?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the first answer that I gave was that that has to do nothing with my -- with my testimony, and the second is that there are information in it that covering a long period of working there, and that they are just under my protection of sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask to you look at what is Rule 65 ter 1D238, Mr. Hutsch. Mr. Hutsch, this is a letter which responds to the Defence request which I showed you last night. It is a letter from Mr. Saxon and dated 20th of April of 2007. You will recall that the point -- the number which related to our request in relation to this notes was number 2. And under number 2, in this response, Mr. Saxon writes that after your contact, Mr. Hutsch refused to provide this material and state that they contain no reference to the event in Ljuboten. So is that what you told the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a very short context, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that, a minute or so ago, you indicated that, in fact, those notes contained inter alia information that pertained to your observation in regards to the event of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, you were requesting all the notes from the 5th up to the 24th of August; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, and your response --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, sorry. And I said that this is a very short, very short sentence of a, what I would say, 45-, 50-minute long phone call, where I exactly expressed, explained why I wouldn't give this material out of my hand. And if I'm counting right, you were asking for material for my investigation notes over 19 days, and just three days or four days were covering the Ljuboten event -- events.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in your discussion with the Prosecutor, and contrary to what are you claiming now, Mr. Hutsch, you told the Prosecution that none of those notes, aside those of the 12 and 14th August which we mentioned we had already, you say contain --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just show me where it is written --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please bring up --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- nowhere is this written in this answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- what is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- because you are concluding my answer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters would say like to ask Mr. Hutsch to observe the pause after the questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch you are being asked to slow down after the question and take a little break before your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In this response, as it is taken the Office of the Prosecutor, it says: "Mr. Hutsch refused to provide these materials and state that they contain no reference to the events in Ljuboten." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's right for all my notes between the 5th and the 10th and the 13th and from the 14th afternoon going up to the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that's, in any case, what not the Prosecutor recorded in this note. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've just made it up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I told Mr. Kuehnel when we had the phone call. On the other hand, Mr. Mettraux, because we are exactly again in the point where you're going to manipulate, just let's come back to yesterday to your cross-examination. Is it right that you cross-examined me to the 10th of August yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I think it is for me to ask the question and not for --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you were --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- you to ask question --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- you were fabricating yesterday with the two testimonies of two witnesses, and you confrontated me with these witnesses. What I did is I was just investigating in the Internet the testimony of these two witnesses. We were discussing yesterday the matter of the 10th of August, and you confrontated me with two testimonies of witnesses from the 11th of August to falsify my testimony. That, Mr. Mettraux, is the reason why we stop in this moment any testimony without a interpreter in German language. And just you confrontated me with the testimony of Mr. Bolton, and it is very clear that Mr. Bolton is speaking about a crowd in content with the 11th of August. Mr. Bolton confirmed that there was a check-point on page 16712, a permanent check-point, like he said, on the street from Radisani to Ljubanci to Ljuboten. He was on page 1668. He said all these events are going on on the 11th of August; and on page 16670, he is describing the crowd as a event of the 11th. And then the witness, who I think M-048, who did his testimony on the 25th, is talking about that there was crowd of 2.000 people on the 11th of August, and I think that is what the people had been in the front of Ljubanci. So what you did yesterday is you made the Chamber believe that my testimony was wrong, but we were just discussing the 10th, and that, Mr. Mettraux, is shameful. You --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- do you agree with me that you are a fabricator.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch we're going to come back to the 12th of August and the issue of the crowd and the statement of Mr. Bolton, because we have located the material that is relevant to this issue. But at this stage, Mr. Hutsch, I will just ask you to answer the questions that are being asked to you. So do you agree, sir, that, in fact, the reality is you have no notes for the period 10 and 11 of August of 2001. That's why you refuse to provide them to the Prosecution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to answer in German.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The position with German interpretation is that limited interpretation will be available tomorrow. It will enable the answers of Mr. Hutsch given in German to be translated into English. It will not allow your questions to be interpreted into German. That is the first and the earliest that it has been possible to arrange for German interpretation. Now, at the moment, Mr. Hutsch, the Chamber, you will appreciate, has heard the evidence. It doesn't interfere with the questions of counsel. It evaluates, in the end, whether there is force in what counsel is putting to you or not. Please understand, therefore, that if there are questions which you think to a impartial audience would not be a fair and balanced question, that the Chamber evaluates that at the end of all the evidence and weighs up the consequences. So don't think because we are silent we know nothing. Secondly, the sort of issue that you're talking about would appear, to me at least - I haven't had a chance to my fellow Judges - but it would appear, to me at least, not really to involve any issue concerning a difference between English and German language, but to involve your concern that Mr. Mettraux' questions are being selective when he picks pieces of evidence that has been given or pieces, or pieces even from a statement of a witness who has not yet given evidence but may come to give evidence. We don't know. You feel that in selecting pieces of that he is putting to you as a fact something which isn't borne out by the actual evidence that has been given. Now that's something that I really don't think involves any difference between English or German. You have just demonstrated how very well alert you are to those issues and your capacity for putting your contrary view, and they are things which we weigh in due course. So can I just leave you with thoughts to reflect upon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I think we all appreciate that you're having to work in a second language and that you're familiarity with that language cannot be as easy as in your first language; but, on the other hand, you are demonstrating a very clear capacity to communicate in English. You may feel that you could do it more readily in German, but you are not being pushed for time. You are given time to think about it and you can take more time, and you can certainly take more time to answer, if you feel you need to have more time. So you don't have to rush with a short answer and then allow the matter to move on. You've taken more time this morning, for example, to go back over yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So we're sitting and we're absorbing and we're weighing up. Be aware of that, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And, of course, Mr. Saxon will be able to re-examine later as well. Carry on, please, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'd like now to turn to what is Exhibit P308, please. This is your reporter's notes of the 12th of August of 2001, and I'd like to go through a few of your annotations in this document. Do you have the document in front of you, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask the registry please to turn to the next page of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch you can see this is the first annotations which is contained in your notes of the 12th of August, and it refers to what you say is a telephone conversation between Mr. Beqiri and there's a number of information. It took place at 7.48 hours, and it refers to a number of events which you can read, including that Ljube Boskoski said to be on his way to Ljuboten. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you ever able to verify the information of Mr. Beqiri or did you take any step to verify this information?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that is the reason why you didn't reproduce this particular exchange in your statement to the Prosecutor, or could it be the reason why you didn't reproduce it in your statement to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next event or indication that I would like to turn to is the one at 8.03 hours. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in there, there's a reference to Hermelin BTR support; and, in the parenthesis, there is a "3." Am I correct to understand that "3" refers to the one Hermelin and two BTR-80, which you referred to in your testimony and in your statement? Is that how it should be understood?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can turn then to the -- the next annotations which is at 8.20 hours, it says: "Carsten telephone MUP attack on direct orders of B, conflict between Ministry of Defence and Ministry of Interior about conduct according to VM," that is Ministry of Defence, "no NLA in Ljuboten." You have indicated that "Carsten" is Carsten Hoffman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Hoffman was and still is a fellow journalist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you ask Mr. Hoffman where he obtained that information from, which you say he transmitted to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't do, because we phoning over cell phone, and it was clear that they were intercepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you were not able to verify the information which was provided --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we please turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, there's an annotation at 8.27 and 8.34.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a annotation of another phone conversation with the same person, Mr. Beqiri of the NLA, and then two annotations the at 9.25 and 9.28. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you refer to information that you received from the army that there was no NLA in the village. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell this Chamber who you received that information from?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we already discussed this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could you give the name of the person who you say gave that you information.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could you indicate what position this person held in the army, you say?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what's the reason, Mr. Hutsch, for you refusing to disclose the name of this person, whom say gave you information?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These persons are still working in the army, and what I think is that they will come under pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, at 9.28, there's another annotations which says, "trying to found out if they are 'Alis,' as printed."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Operation supposedly only by the MUP." Do you recall who you say you received that information from?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall whether that person was in any position of authority or any particular institution that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall what institution that would be?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you or can you not recall what institution?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall the position of that person?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall the identity of is this person?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, I will ask to you look at the next annotations in these notes, Mr. Hutsch. This is that is made at 9.48 hours, and it says: "Telephone Ejup Hamiti, they -- or we are trying to leave village through river-bed, going to Radisani, OSCE not allowed into the village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall having had that phone conversation with Mr. Hamiti that morning?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me. It was my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall if it was your interpreter that called Mr. Hamiti or the other way around? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, it's, again, a false story, isn't it, and one that you picked up from the Human Rights Watch report. Is that correct, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I would like to show you what is Exhibit P3252, please. This is it, again, the report of Human Rights Watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like the registry, please, to turn to page U000-0111, please, and I'd like the registry, please, to focus on the middle of the page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you look at the centre of the page, Mr. Hutsch, you will see there's an indented part of the document, which starts with the words, "Because of the big offensive." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it starts like this, it says this: "Because of the big offensive, we left the village and headed for Skopje. We headed down to the river as bullets were flying over our heads; then we had to stop by the river. We couldn't go farther down because we would have reached Radisani. We heard that the OSCE buses were not allowed to come into the village by the police. "Then, after some of my cousins spoke on the phone, we headed towards the asphalt road. We went one by one because there were many old people and children and we had to help them to the main road from the river." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's where you took your story from, isn't it, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, your conclusion presented as fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you a question, Mr. Hutsch. Is that correct that you took that story and implanted it in your note from the Human Rights Watch report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Hutsch, there's a person who has testified before this Tribunal about this particular incident or this particular event.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is transcript of the 24th of August of 2007 at page 4094.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he was asked, Mr. Hutsch, whether he or Mr. Hamiti, who was with him at the time, did any phone call at the time when they were going around or along the river, as described in this document. And the question was this. It is at line 23: "You describe, at paragraph 32, that somebody from this group around Ejup received a phone call, telling them there were a lot of angry Macedonian villagers from Radisani waiting outside Radisani," and we're talking about the 12th of August, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is not mentioned there, but --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- it says -- well, we'll come to the time in a minute, sir, because that is going to be the next issue. "Do you recall saying that?" "Yes I do." "Can you now recall who among the group received that phone call? "I couldn't say for sure, because many people had phone, mobile phones, that they kept talking all the time. And how to say it, I said that. We heard that it was dangerous to go in the direction of Radisani, because people there were very angry, so we should change course. "And is that correct, however, and to the extent that you can recall, Mr. Murati, is that correct that it was neither you, nor Ejup Hamiti, who received phone call? Can you recall that? And the answer of this person was: "Neither of us had a phone." So, do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that you made up that story based on the Human Rights Watch report, thinking that you were safe claiming that they had mobile phone access, since it was mentioned in the Human Rights report? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you show me where I wrote that it was a mobile phone connection that with we had with Mr. Hamiti?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you suggesting that as he was walking down the river, trying to escape the village, he had a fixed phone with him, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you show me where in writing that Mr. Hamiti was still on his way? As far as I remember, in my German notes, I wrote that he planned to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, your description of it, Mr. Hutsch, is that they were going at the time: "They are -- we are trying to leave village through river-bed going to Radisani." That's what you said, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you show me the German translation? Probably, it will become much more clearer in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, it's Exhibit P308. This is -- in the German version, this is N003-0009, in the German. Do you have that in front of you, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. So what I see is I wrote in German: [Foreign language spoken]. So, at 9.48, Mr. Hamiti is describing a plan that isn't still realised because we have the word "versuiten." I don't know if Mr. Hamiti was still at his house in this time or whether he was going; but, again, you are presenting your conclusions as facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm not presenting anything as fact --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are doing --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- Mr. Hutsch. The question was asked also of Mr. Ejup Hamiti. The problem you is not only the existence, or otherwise, of a phone available to Mr. Hamiti, but also about the timing, at which you say this conversation took place, and you say 9.48. I will read out to what you ask about the time what Mr. Murati said about that. He was asked: "And I think you had indicated to the Prosecutor that you went down the stream with Ejup at around 12.45 to 1.00, approximately; is that correct?" "Yes." "And is that correct also that you went down the stream on that day with Ejup only on one occasion; is that correct?" "It is." So the truth is, Mr. Hutsch, is that you didn't know the time at which they had attempted to make that walk down the stream, because it wasn't mentioned in the Human Rights Watch report. You thought you were safe mentioning that time in your note, but, in fact, it did not happen at 9.48 but at a time between 12.45 and 1.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, at, let's say, 10.00, this group around Ejup Hamiti could create this plan that they realised between 12.45 and 1.00. Well, it is your conclusion, like all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you, sir, that it is, again, one of the things you fabricated in those notes, and I would like to turn to another one.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to hear the word fabricate not of you, because you were fabricating yesterday a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's look at the next entry on your notes. It's a reference to the information press office of the Ministry of Interior, something that says, "Ljube on his way to Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we turn forward to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, at 11.23 hours, there's, "information press centre, Ministry of Interior, Boskoski in Ljuboten." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that, during your examination-in-chief, there was some discussion about the information which you claimed to have received from the press information office of the Ministry of Interior. I believe that what you said was that you were unable to provide the names of the employees of the press office information of the MOI because you did not know them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, because I didn't have a discussion with them. That was part of the work of my interpreter, of my Macedonian interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that you claimed to have had many or frequent contacts with the MOI press information office on the 11th of August. That would be the Saturday. Do you recall saying that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, sir, is that you had no such contacts; and by "you," I mean neither you or the person whom you say accompanied you with the MOI press information centre. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason why you didn't have any such contacts, Mr. Hutsch, is that at the time, in Macedonia and in the Ministry of Interior, there was no such thing as a press information office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some spokespersons. If they were really established as a press information centre, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the thing is, in your statement, Mr. Hutsch, you told the Office of the Prosecutor that, at this stage, you would -- you did not know the names of those people you said had you talked to, but that you would undertake to do so in the future. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if I was asked again, I will -- I will give a phone call to my interpreter and ask him if he remembers who he spoke to; but, on the other hand, you will say there were no spokesperson for the Ministry of Interior in this time. Is that what you would like to say now?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, isn't that correct --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, Mr. Hutsch. It is not for me to answer your question. Is that correct, Mr. Hutsch, that you were actually asked by the Defence to provide a great number of references to the people who you say you talked to, information on 24 different issues, and that you refused almost to all of them to provide that information? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, not to all of them, Mr. Hutsch. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So why do you ask incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Almost all of them, I said. But I will direct your attention more specifically to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could see Rule 65 ter 236, please, and if we can turn to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This was the letter sent by the Defence to the OTP asking them to provide us with information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if could you look at the third page, this would be 1D00-2657.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, if you look at paragraph 13, please, 1-3, it says that: "In his statement of 25th to 27th of August, 2005, at paragraph 85, Mr. Hutsch says that at 10.07 a.m." That is the same note as in your notes, "he had a phone call with the press information office of the MOI. "The Defence wishes to receive from you the name of the person whom Mr. Hutsch says he talked to on that occasion. If Mr. Hutsch cannot remember the name of that person, we ask you to obtain the name from the legal -- language assistant, which is said to have had that phone conversation." That's what we asked the Prosecution. Do you recall what you answered to that question when it was asked of you, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can look at Rule 65 ter 1D238, at point 13, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The record that was made of your conversation with Mr. Kuehnel is this: "With to the representative of the Ministry of Interior, Mr. Hutsch did not record the name of this person. Mr. Hutsch simply refers to he or she as the ministry spokesperson." So at the time, when you were being queried by the Prosecution about this matter, you didn't offer to make a phone call to find out who this person was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason why you didn't make that offer, Mr. Hutsch, is because there is no such person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is your conclusion again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I would like you to have a look at Rule 65 ter 1D310, please. What will appear in front of you, Mr. Hutsch, is a statement by a person called Tatania Najdovska-Trajkovska, which was taken by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski. And if you can look at the first paragraph, you will see what -- that we made the request; paragraph 2 contains her details; paragraph 3 contains her current occupation; and I would like to start at paragraph 4. This person says this: "Starting in May 2001, I worked for a period as the Chef de cabinet of the Minister of the Interior, Ljube Boskoski." Paragraph 5, it says: "When the Interior Ministry spokesperson, Stevi Pandorovksi, resigned from his post at the end of May or the beginning of June, 2001, I cannot recall the exact date, I became the only person responsible for dealing on behalf of the Minister with questions from journalists and the media in general. "I began to take care of relations with the media, while Mr. Pandorovski was still there, because the Minister was not satisfied with his work. Then Minister, Mr. Boskoski, wanted as much information as possible to be published in the media and was not satisfied with Mr. Pandorovski in that respect. "In August 2001, Mr. Pandorovski had not been replaced, and I was effectively doing his job as a spokesperson. Ms. Natalia Ivceva also had several responsibilities regarding contact with the media. Ms. Ivceva dealt especially with issues of a international character. When journalists were in questions, we sometimes worked together. "In my work, I had frequent and regular contacts with Macedonian and foreign journalists. I was the person whom journalists usually called when they needed information on the activities of the Ministry. "I never had contacts with any one named Franz-Josef Hutsch. This is the first time that I have heard his name." I will stop there for a second to ask you this, Mr. Hutsch: Is that correct that in Macedonia, in the year of 2001, and to work as a journalist you were required to register yourself with the then Ministry of Information, which would then allow to you obtain certain passes to go around the country? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that, but I didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's correct you never registered yourself as a journalist? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- well, let's go on reading --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In Macedonia. Let's go on reading the statement of Ms. Najdrovska-Trajkovska. She says this: "Asked by the Defence, I confirmed that in August of 2001, or throughout 2001, there never was a Ministry of Interior press and information centre. When journalists needed information, they contacted me. "Asked by the Defence, I can say that I was not contacted by any journalist or the interpreter of any journalist on 10, 11, or 12 August, 2001, in regard to what happened in Ljuboten village. "Asked by the Defence, the practice of the Ministry of Interior was not to publish information on ongoing operations. Information was released after the completions of operations." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, there was, as Ms. Najdovska-Trajkovska mentioned, never any press centre that you or your interpreter could have contacted. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written it has not press information centre, yes. We are, again, in a semantic discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And also what can you inferred from that statement, at the least, is that that's not the person whom you say your assistant talked to. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's done by witness that is close to the accused, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what do you mean by that Mr. Hutsch? Do you mean that she is wasn't being truthful?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are perfect in conclusions; not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think it may interest the Trial Chamber, not myself, Mr. Hutsch, to know what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just looking to that, that a person, a witness, Ms. Najdovska-Trajkovska, is giving a statement on your request for your accused that promoted her.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you think that this renders her unable to tell the truth, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But not more than, for example my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you should give us the name of this interpreter, Mr. Hutsch, so that we can verify the reliability of that person. Would you like to do so now?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, after a lot of people in Macedonian became a lot of trouble because they were potential witnesses for this case, I never will hand over the name of my interpreters. There's a responsibility that is a little bit stronger than your tricks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Hutsch. Could you explain what you mean by my "tricks"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your tricks is that you confrontate me with testimony and quotes by other witnesses that are nothing to deal with the thing that we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see, Mr. Hutsch. Well, we'll turn to another statement which might assist you further.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is at Rule 65 ter 1D338, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what will appear in front of you, Mr. Hutsch, is a statement of a person called Natalia Ivceva, which is the person to whom Mrs. Najdovska-Trajkovska was referring. As you can see, it is a statement given by Natalia Ivceva. It is dated 26th of April, 2007. It is, again, a statement was taken by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski. And if you look at paragraph 1, you will have her details; and paragraph 2, the fact that we asked her to provide information; and in paragraph 3, the place or the position which she held at the time in August of 2001. It is that she worked for "the Ministry of Interior as assistant minister for International Cooperation and European integration." "In the organisational set up, I was in charge of the sector which was directly subordinated to the Ministry. And then at paragraph 4, Ms. Ivceva says this: "In this capacity, alongside other work the job entailed, I was in contact with journalists, both Macedonian and foreign. Journalists usually addressed requests for information to the Minister, whether verbally or in written from. If these requests refers to the Minister's activities, I would forward them to the head of office or to the Minister directly, depending on the nature of the request." "Tatania Najdovska-Trajkovska was the Interior Minister's head of office and was at the same time the person from the Ministry of Interior authorised for contacts with the press." Then at paragraph 6, it say this: "I do not know -- sorry, "in 2001, we did not have a press centre or press information centre at the MOI. Statements and information came from the Minister's office. I do not know a journalist by the name of France Joe Hutsch, and I do not remember ever being in contact with a person with this name or anyone who was petitioned me on his behalf. "I was not in touch with a single journalist or a interpreter working for a journalist on 10, 11, and 12 August 2001, with regard to the events in Ljuboten." So here, again, Mr. Hutsch, we have the only other person working in relation to press matter in context with journalists at the relevant time; and not only has she never heard of you, but she makes it clear that she was never contacted on the 10, 11 or 12th of August, with regard to the events of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, probably, you can explain who was dealing with all the press questions and requests concerning the mine incident in Ljuboten. Who was doing that and who was satisfying the interest of journalists all over the world in that thing? Because both spokespersons of the Ministry of Interior, they don't give any statement to that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, I will ask you to focus on this question. We asked the witness, or this person in any case, about the events of the 10th, 11th and 12th of August, and the only matter that is of concern at this stage is your suggestion that you or your interpreter contacted the press information centre or a spokesperson, someone you claimed to have been a spokesperson, of the MOI on the 12th, but also on the 11th of August of 2001. But, in fact, I'm putting it to you that you never had such contacts, Mr. Hutsch. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is incorrect. Like I said, and if you just go in a logical way, a little bit deeper, then you will find that we have had a incident at the 10th at 8.20. That was the reason that we have had a Ljuboten incident in general. What you are trying to present to the Chamber is that there was no press and information contact because both spokespersons that you present here say there were no contact to a single journalist or interpreter with these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask it another way, Mr. Hutsch. Do you have anyone that can you name from the Ministry of Interior who you say was contacted by you or by your language assistants on the 11th or the 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about the 10th, the 11th, and the 12th. Like I said, it's something that I have to -- to ask my language assistant. Probably he knows; probably he doesn't know. I don't know. But definitely he was doing phone calls, and he was passing this information to me, like I was writing that in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is: No, you are unable to provide the name of any one person within the Ministry of Interior whom you say had you contact with or your language assistants or 11th or 12th of August, 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. In this moment, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to go back or go forward in time on that day. Do you remember saying in your evidence in chief that you, at first, were in the first observation point, and that at a certain point in time you moved to a different location. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at -- on the 27th of June of this year, at page 2724 to 2727, you said that you moved from point 1 to point 2, at around 8.30, and reach point 2 at around 8.45 or 9.00. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you explained that the reason for you to move from observation point 1 to observation point 2 was that, from approximately 8.30 onwards, could you not follow what was going on in the village because there was a hill which was blocking your view. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So can you just say how you went from observation point 1 to observation point 2? Did you go by foot, by car?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: By car.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that you mention -- you had mentioned originally that the time at which you had travelled or moved from observation point 1 to observation point 2 had taken place, not at 8.30 as you said in your evidence in chief, but at 10.45. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the first time you suggested that the time had been incorrect was during a proofing session with the Prosecution on the 19th of June of 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the reason why you changed the time in your evidence is because you realized that some the observations, which you claim would you have been able to do from observation point 1 during the period between 8.30 and 10.45, could in fact not be made from that point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Hutsch, to say that you had kept your notes in chronological order. You said that to the Court yesterday again. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also say that on the transcript of the 26th of June of 2007, at page 2693, you said this: "I was using a notebook or, yeah, a notebook, where I wrote in all the things that I saw in the moment when I took it, when I saw it. And I had a time so that I watch first my clock, I wrote the time inside, and then I wrote the notes that I was seeing in this moment." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we look, again, please, at what is exhibit P308, that's, again, your reporter's notes, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask the registry to go to the sixth page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of the English and it's also the bottom of the German in fact, there's an annotation at 11.00 hours: Explosions, RPG, MG-80, fire, northern part Ljuboten, slowly." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page, it goes on to say: "Moving south, nine houses burning. Reinforcements approximately one platoon from Ljubanci to Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that it's in fact the first annotations which you made in your notes from your new observation post?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux. Since yesterday, you don't want to accept that there's a combination between a map and a notebook, and what you are doing now is you present just this notebook without the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting it to you to you, Mr. Hutsch, is, there again, you are making things up. The reason for it being that the events which you recounted in your statements, which you say you observed between the time 8.27, in particular to 9.17 - it's at paragraph 76 to 80 of your statement - you could not have observed them. But I will read a paragraph to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can show what is Rule 65 ter 1D234, please, and if the registry could please go to page 12 that's 1D00-2578. Perhaps we can start with the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will see, it's the previous page referred to 8.27 hours and then 9.17 hours, and then you recount a number of incidents in paragraph 77, 78, and 79.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if you go to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a reference to you're notation at 11.00, which I have just read out to you, and I asked you whether that was your first annotation from your new from your new position, and you said, "No, Mr. Mettraux." But at paragraph 86, of your statement, it say this: "11 hours, this is the first entry in my notebook which was done from a new observation post." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this notebook, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was the question before, Mr. Hutsch, and it say this: "Due to the above mentioned problems, I could not see a part of the progress of the attack because my view was blocked by the hill 631. I moved now directly on the hill 631. I marked this position on attachment PP5, titled 'second part of attack, 11.00 hours,'" and then there's a sentence, and you said: "I moved there at around 10.45." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, that is what you told the Prosecution originally, and perhaps we can show you what is now Exhibit P315, please. Do you recall being shown that picture by the Prosecution, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is a picture that was presented by -- or prepared by you, I'm sorry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can see on the top right-hand corner of the picture, that's the picture which you prepared, and it says: "My observation point -- position," I'm sorry, "from around 10.45 hours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's again what you told the Prosecution at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And only later, when you realised that the original position, as you say you had, did not allow you to observe what you say you observe, have you change your version and placed the time to 8.30. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that directly contradicts your notes, is that correct, which mentions that your first observation on that day from that position was at 11.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux. It doesn't contradict my -- my notes. It contradicts my reminding. And as far as I know, Mr. Saxon sent you a memo where I was correcting my -- my testimony on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you were correcting, Mr. Hutsch, as in another respect, as we will come now, is things which you had come to realise were false and could be exposed as such. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at another one. It's not a important one, perhaps, but it is a telling one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D234, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is, again, your statement, Mr. Hutsch, the statement of 25, 26, 27 of August of 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to turn to page 6 of the statement. This is at 1D00-2572, and if we could focus, please, on paragraph 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this refers to what you say happened on the 11th of August, 2001. That's the Saturday, and it relates in particular to what you say happened at a alleged check-point in Radisani. I will read out to you what paragraph 34 says: "We negotiated with police officers to allow to us pass. The morale and conduct of these people were not good. It was clear to me that around six of these persons were police reservists and two of them were regular police officers." And then you say: "After we gave some bottles of beer and bribing them with 20 euros, we were allowed to pass." Can you see that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that, in a similar proofing note that was provided to the Defence, you suggested a correction to that particular paragraph. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the correction was that, in fact, you hadn't given 20 euros to the police officers but 50 Deutschemark. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason for you to do that, Mr. Hutsch, is that not only was your original version improbable, but it was openly false. Is that why you changed it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's your conclusion again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the reason why you changed is that on the 11th of August, there was no such thing as the euro. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you realised that, you changed your version to the DM, the Deutschemark. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that means that the investigator also is involved in this big mysterious theatre?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's your view, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's your view.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There are other problems, Mr. Hutsch, many other problems with your statements and the evidence which you have sought to give to this Chamber, and there's only a few that we will have the time to go through together. One of them has to do with your observations that you made about what you say was mortar fire, and I'm talking of the 12th of August of 2001. Do you recall making a annotation or, I believe, the first annotation which you made in your notes of fire activity witnessed personally by you at 0803. And if you need me to show you the notes, I will certainly do so.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that I was writing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you said at 8.03 is that what you witnessed at the time was mortar fire from the army, directed into position in or around the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, did you see at about the same time any mortar coming from positions that were not army positions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were coming mortar fire from outside the village, north of the village, as far as I know, or I remember into the village, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you become aware or did you -- were you aware at the time that some of the mortar fire that was directed towards the village had come from NLA positions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So was it your belief at the time, as far as the record that you've made for these proceedings, that all fire had come from the army?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you later become aware - and I'm talking after this period, the August of 2001 - did you become aware that actually some of the fire had come from the NLA? Did you ever become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if witnesses were to testify in this case that, in fact, several of the mortars, which were fired around that time, did not come from army positions, as you say, but had been fired onto the village by NLA positions, you would have seen none of that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, simply for the record, I refer to the transcript 7th of June, 2007, 1674 to 1675; and also the evidence of M-083, 25th of May, 2007, page 1494 to 1495, 1516; and also M-053, 13th of June, 1993, 1994, also 2001 to 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I would like to show you another document, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this would be Exhibit 1D23, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is, Mr. Hutsch, a so-called spot report. This is prepared by the OSCE and is dated Skopje, 14th of August of 2001. It is provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go down to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the section under the subheading "Central Area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it talks about the events of Ljuboten; I mean, as can you see from the rest of the document. And if you can locate a paragraph which starts with the word, "It now seems clear." Can you see that? Can you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "It now seems clear that ethnic Albanian armed group mortar fire brought to bear on to the ethnic Macedonian part of the village originally sparked the fighting, and at least a covert presence of EAAG, did in fact exist in the village." My question is simply were you aware of any of the information contained in that document at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is 1D24, please, Exhibit 1D24.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is another document prepared by the OSCE. It's another report, and this one is a special report about the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask the registry, please, to turn to the third page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask to you locate a paragraph that starts with the words, "On 12 August at 0805 hours." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it say this: "On 12 August at 0805 hours, the first mortar round fell on the village. It landed in the vicinity of the orthodox church in the Macedonian section of the village. Two more rounds followed, each closer to the church. All three are believed to have been 120-millimetres mortars. These are more likely to have been EAAG rounds than government, and were the first shot fired into the village. Thereafter, the army fired on the Albanian side of the village with smaller calibre mortar." Mr. Hutsch, I'll, again, ask you the same question: At the time were you aware of any such information?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please now be shown what is -- Rule 65 ter 1D507, and I'd like the registry --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, first, this is a statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor. It's dated the 27th of October of 2003, and it is taken from a person called Suad Saliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry please to move to page 4 of that document, and if you could please focus on paragraph 9 and enlarge it somewhat.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This the statement of Mr. Suad Saliu, Mr. Hutsch, and he at the time was a member of the so-called 114th Brigade of the NLA. That is what he said: "As Macedonian forces were about to enter the village, Hoxha and Limaj ordered to open mortar fire. They obviously discussed the situation with Bushi, with whom they were in contact on mobile phone. "About six or seven mortar rounds were fired. Our mortars targeted the army positions. I think that five round missed the target, while two hit the army positions." And then he says that "Macedonian security forces were beating the villagers of Ljuboten. And after the mortar rounds impacted, Macedonian security forces started to withdraw from the village." Sir, did you see any of those six or seven mortars to which Mr. Saliu is referring?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the mortars. I just saw the impacts in the area of the orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you relies at that time that they had been coming from the NLA positions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated, I believe, in your statement, and again in your evidence, that at some stage, in mid-September of 2001, you say you were then employed by the embassy -- the German embassy in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have also indicated, I believe, that your superior, direct or incompetent direct - you may specify this - was a person called Peter Matthiesen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your role, in your capacity in this job, I suppose, I will ask you: Did you have access to any sort of intelligence collected by the embassy or Mr. Matthiesen at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you discuss at any point your visit or what you say were your visits in Ljuboten with him?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did Mr. Matthiesen share with you what he knew of those events as well?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some parts of that what he knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did he share with you that he knew that the NLA had tried to capture the village on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did he tell you that the first few mortars that had been fired on to Ljuboten had come from the NLA positions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 1D224. There's an original in German, Mr. Hutsch. I will give you the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, you can look at the German one which appears to be a better or more accurate record of what happened. This is a document dated 16 August of 2001, and it is written by -- it comes from the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany. It says, "Military attache, Lieutenant-Colonel Peter H. Matthiesen," on the top-left corner. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it has a subheading saying, "Information on Ljuboten." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a general paragraph, under the subheading "General," which is a sort of a brief summary of some comments of Mr. Matthiesen. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then, if you go down to the next section of that document, there's a subheading saying, "Two Accounts of Events." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the first paragraph, it says: "The NLA, National Liberation Army, tried to capture the town in several hit and run attempts but was prevented from doing so by Macedonian security forces." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he says that: "The attack by security forces of 12th August was led by the Macedonian part of the town against the centre of the town." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then a sentence, if you can look at the German, starts with the word: [Foreign language spoken]. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in the English, there was a typo because the sentence should read: "There is no doubt that first three mortar attacks were aimed at the security forces." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: "It was the Macedonian forces which then followed by using further mortars." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's information which your superior, Mr. Matthiesen, had not shared with you, Mr. Hutsch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another issue which I would like to raise with you, another observation which you made about what you said you saw at the time. You've given evidence here about this on the 26th of June of 2007 at page 2698. Do you recall that you gave a indication to the Prosecution that you remembered that some of the mortars that had been used, you believed, by the army used a system of delayed ignition. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that, in fact, you never see or you never saw such a thing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, another witness came to testify in this court, a member of the army, Mr. Hutsch, and he was asked about this particular material or this particular ammunition that you say wasn't used on that day. That's witness M-083. It is on 27th of August of 2007. It's at page 4185 to 4186. I will just read it out to you. The question is this: "The army had, on these positions, 82-millimetres and 120-millimetre grenade launchers. Is that correct?" And then the question continues: "Can you concur with me that these units that were in the village of Ljuboten near the army of the Republic of Macedonia at the time, in August 2001, did not have nor did they use mortared grenade with delayed," and then it says "ignition." It should have said "ignition." And then he said: "No, no. There was no way that this would be the case. We never had such shells. We never used them." So, in fact, and contrary to what you claim, Mr. Hutsch, there could not have been such shell because they were simply not in use in the Macedonian army at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But are you falsifying, again, what I said, because I said that I didn't see the impacts. That means the impact flash on the ground, and that my conclusion from that was that they were using shells with -- with delay ignitions. So it was just my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what you said is this. It is at page 2698 on the 26th of June 2007: "Did you notice anything in particular about the impacts or the explosions of these shells?" "What I think is that they were using delayed igniters." "Ignitors, you mean?" "Yes." "Which is the same as detonators?" "Yes." And then there is an exchange with the interpreter, and Mr. Saxon goes on to ask: "The so-called delayed ignitor or detonator, how did they work?" "They are working in a way that the explosion is going around 15 up to 20 metres over the target. So that means, especially, if you are -- if you look -- like to destroy so-called soft targets, you have a bigger circle on the ground to hit them." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I feel confirmed because I said what I think is that they were using "delayed ignitors."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But again, Mr. Hutsch, you making a statement about things without verifying them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complete investigation going on to Ljuboten is based -- that's the reason why it never was published because I never investigated to the end. I don't have a point of view what was going on in Ljuboten at that day. That's what I was writing there in my notes, and that's what I saw. I didn't confirm whether if there was any -- I didn't confirm any one of the phone call, one of the speeches, one of the other guys told me. I didn't investigate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't it be the truth, Mr. Hutsch, that the reason why you never published the piece about this event was because you were not there. You never entered the village on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's your conclusion again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We were running on for extra time to meet your convenience, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly, in that case, I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you recall that you told the Office of the Prosecutor that you understood the operation to have finished at 12.15. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can take to you your statement for a second, once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's Rule 65 ter 1D234.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to take you to paragraph 94 of your statement, which would be at page 13, 1-3, of your statement, and it is page 1D00-2579.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please focus on paragraph 94, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, you said the following to the Office of the Prosecutor, it says this: "Between 1330 and 1450 hours, I left my observation position and was driving towards Radisani. I was driving into the direction of Skopje. We went from there on the road connecting Skopje and Ljuboten. Along this road was another check-point. We approached this check-point from the south side." Just so that we understand the path that you say you took there, is it the fact that you actually went back down the road through Radisani, which you had used that morning, towards Skopje and then return towards the village from the south side, I believe you said. Is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we went to Skopje and from then we went north to Ljuboten and another -- another village close to the village Skopje Rastak, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on your way down to go to Skopje, you went through Radisani, as you had, you say, on the way up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were passing Radisani, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you notice anything abnormal or out of the ordinary when you went down at that time, or was it the same as when you came in?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Radisani, there were some people in the street listening to that what was going on in -- in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you notice anything else, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see perhaps a crowd - I'm using the word "crowd"- of angry civilians?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the outskirt, yeah, in the outskirt, at the entrance of Radisani, but a crowd? There were some people there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Hutsch, this is the crowd of people which we were discuss being yesterday, and I'm going to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 1D925.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So I'll go through first through the first page with you. This is a daily log sheet; and as you can see, it's dated the 12th of August of 2001. It has come in the hands of the Defence from the Prosecution. And if you look at the bottom of the page, please, you will see it comes from the archives of the OSCE mission in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go back up this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will see there are a number of columns at the top. Can you see that? It says, "Ser, time, source," and so on. Can you see those?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to draw your attention to the fourth fifth and sixth column. It says, "event, remarks, and action." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the fourth page of that document, I'll ask you to look at the annotations under number 23 of that document, please. Under the column events, it says this: "Reports that 200 plus refugees from Ljuboten are on their way from the village to Radisani." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then under remark, there's a annotation which says: "They are moving from Ljuboten south-west in direction Radisani by following the river.
