At the entrance of Radisani, near the bridge, grid 371591, a crowd is gathered with iron pipes in their hands waiting for the refugees." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in the last column which is action, it says: "Team will meet the refugees together with ICRC on their way along the river." It says: "CMC," that is the Crisis Management Centre, "was informed about the crowd at the bridge. The later body promised to send a police team on that particular spot." So that crowd of people, Mr. Hutsch, this is -- or those would be the people whom you should have known had you gone through on that day, as you claim you did. That's the group of people to whom Mr. Bolton referred, Is that correct, and which you never mentioned in your own statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I never asked what was going on in Radisani; second, like I quoted, Mr. Bolton was talking about a crowd on page 1670 on his testimony. This incident is located on the 11th of August, and we were discussing all these matters around the 10th, because we were just discussing the 10th yesterday. You were confrontating me with this in combination with the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's not correct, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What happened is this: You were read not the passage which you are now referring to. You are correct. The passage you are referring to refers to the 11th. The passage which was read to you of Mr. Bolton's evidence was of the 12th, and what I'm putting to you now is that as referred by Mr. Bolton, although he didn't use the word "crowd" in relation to the 12th, is the same group of people that is referred here in the report of the OSCE. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's a group of people which you had made no mention of in your statement, any of your statement, and yesterday took issue with the suggestion that, in fact, there was a crowd there Radisani. You also mentioned a particular location at the bridge in Radisani. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 10th. We were discussing the 10th, the Friday --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and you were confronting me exactly with this point. You were making me believe, or you tried to make me believe, that that happened on Friday, not on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, what I'm putting to you is that had you been where you said at the time, you would have seen a huge crowd of people armed with iron pipes and other items, and you not have been able, as you said, to travel where you said you did. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Hutsch, this evidence is also reiterated by other witnesses who have testified in this trial: Witness M84 at page 1498 on the 25th of May. He was talking against of the 12th of August, and he says: "During that time from the village, from Radisani, hundreds, maybe more, people were running with shovels, with forks, with axes, with hunting guns. They were running down to fight with the population from Ljuboten." You could not have missed that, Mr. Hutsch, had you been there. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, there is not a line how long this operation takes; second, as far as I know, we have a report that 200 plus refugees from Ljuboten on the way from the village to Radisani; and, then, we have another crowd that is moving from Radisani to the north. It is not written here where exactly, first, that happened; second I know that they are -- I think it was in a story from Vojska Naki from the World Newspaper. This incident is mentioned, so it was known to me that something happened like that, but I didn't have a own -- an own eye on confrontation between villagers of Ljuboten and villagers of Radisani. What I saw is that there were people in the street. They were angry,, they had things in their hands, yes, but I didn't see a confrontation; and the second is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I will stop you here. You are making things up, aren't you? You mentioned this nowhere, nowhere in your statement, not in the first one, not in the second one, not in the three proofings with you had the Prosecution. What you are doing now, Mr. Hutsch, is you're trying to mold your story to evidence with which you are confronted. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, if I read yesterday these two testimonies of the two -- two witnesses in a right way, there were a lot of things they didn't say because they never were asked. I can just tell you that when I was giving my first testimony, you will exactly that there is difference between the two testimonies I gave to the Prosecution. First is that what I saw myself in the time from 10th up to the 12th, or 14th if you want so; and the second was what I was doing when I was member of the German embassy. We had to wait for waiver that was coming from the German Ministry of Defence in this time. That was the reason for the second meeting. And if you see that especially on the events of the 12th what was going on in Ljuboten, we was going on, I will say, in the night up to 11.30, 12.00, 1.00, I think, I left the Tribunal. I wasn't asked. And if you start in the morning at 8.00 and you are giving this testimony to the Prosecution, because we were under time pressure as now as well, I didn't -- I didn't mention that. And if I remember right, and if I recall my testimony with Mr. Saxon, he didn't ask me as well. You are the first who is asking me in this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is your evidence this, Mr. Hutsch: Now you claim that you that you, in fact, saw angry villagers with axes and other instrument, as is clear from this document, hundreds of them, on the road which you claim you passed, including the very bridge which you mentioned, and you did not make a note of that or did not think it was relevant, when in fact it would have prevented you from going where you say you go. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, the road wasn't blocked; second, I didn't see hundreds of them; third, there is no time when this crowd disappeared or was destroyed, and there is no, as far as I see, any mark or any notice what happened with this crowd. We have just that at 12.50, a source, "C-2," reports that that happened and that happened. What I think is there were no direct observation from an OSCE member, because he said, in results, the team will meet the refugees together with ICRC. So what I didn't see, and I can't say that, I didn't see a confrontation between villagers, and that people have been in the street if you are just going - you have to pick me up - but, for example, the road up to Blace in the same time was blocked by the Macedonian World Congress, if I'm right. Also, a crowd of people that changed between 150 and, I would say, up to 3.000, it was normal. Things like that have been normal, that angry people have been in the street, for example, in front of the parliament. These days with a lot of people and angry crowd, it was normal. It was --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Hutsch, I will stop there. Yesterday, when I asked you those questions, you took issues with the suggestions that I made that there was a crowd of people and accused me to have misled the Chamber about this; therefore, suggesting, at the least, that this wasn't true. Is that correct, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were telling me that happened on 10th, that means on Friday. Now you present another document that happens on Sunday. So we were discussing yesterday the Friday, and you confrontated me with material that you said that belongs to the Friday, and there was not such a evidence on Friday. There was --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- not such a incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, you were being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we're going to have to interrupt this conversation, Mr. Mettraux. We have run on a little longer in the expectation it might finish, but not so. We must break now and will resume at a quarter past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'd like to move on to a different point. But before we do that, I would simply like to come back on two statements which you made. You recall just before that you suggested that you were asked questions about this crowd in Radisani, in relation to the 10th of August, and that I tried to mislead you, and also that the statement of Mr. Bolton referred to not the 12th but the 10th. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I draw your attention to the transcript. It is of yesterday at page 6206, and it starts at line 8. This is my question --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it possible to show yesterday's transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So I think you will have to believe my reading, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very difficult, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, it reads like that. The question is: "Well, first, I'll ask you this."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can manage it, Mr. Mettraux, with some difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be wonderful. It would be page 6206, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask to you look at line number 8, Mr. Hutsch. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have page 6206 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask to you look at line 10 on that page. It reads like that. That was my question: "Well, first, I'll ask you this. You've indicated that at the check-point on that day, on the 12th, you saw a number of policemen, and I think you mentioned a number. Did you see anyone else at what you call the check-point?" And you answer: "Just police officers." And then I go on to say: "Well, you see, this evidence is directly contradicted, once again, by the evidence of another witness, who has already given evidence in this case and who had come precisely from the village of Radisani on that very day and who went towards the village of Ljuboten." And I continue: "But contrary to you, this person did not mention any check-point in Radisani, but what he mentioned is that there was a immense crowd of civilians is there. So you I would agree that what he saw," and then I said: "Your Honour, that would be Mr. Bolton. It is on 7th of June, 2007, page 1686 to 1687." But before I proceed to Mr. Bolton, do you agree that it was clear that I was asking you about the 12th not the 10th, as you seem to allege this morning. Do you agree Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree, because if we're going up a little bit more up in this testimony or in this page, you will see that we were just discussing the 10th, and I didn't check in this moment that you were talking about the 12th. That is, again, one of the -- the points that I would like to answer in German. We were just discussing the matter on Friday. If we are going upstairs, you will find that you said: "Let's come to the Friday," things like that, and you just put in, in this question, the 12th. We were discussing the complete Friday incidents, and you put in line number 9 and, I didn't check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, all of the previous questions that came before this one related to your annotations on the 12th of August, including at 6.03 in the morning and 7.11. And, on that page, it is very clear that it refers to not to the 10th, as you seem to allege, to explain the problems with your evidence; but starting at page 6203 and goes on to the page that I read to you, it is the 12th. The accusation which you've made and the allegation that you're, in fact, talking about the 10th and not the 12th is just another invention to get out of your lies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to show you also the statement of Mr. Bolton, which I've cited to you at the time. It was 7 of June of 2007, and I mention in the transcript it was page 1686 to 1687. And in the middle of page, it starts in those words, that's a question: "Sir, we left off at 12th of August, and I would just like to ask you two or three more questions about that day. The first one is: You would confirm that did you not enter the village on that day. Is that correct?" "That's correct." "And do you understand properly that the reason why you did not or could not enter the village on that day was because of the animosity of the civilians, or some civilians in any case, that were around the village, and the animosity which they showed to your team. Is that correct?" "There was, when we tried to approach the village initially. Right at the beginning, following the mine strike, there was animosity from the villagers in Ljubanci. Subsequently, we did not meet with animosity when trying to approach Ljuboten from the other direction which was further to the east avoiding Ljubanci," and then it goes on. The rest of the passage is at the next page that I've read to you, but I want to save time here. Do you agree, again, Mr. Hutsch, that the passage which I read to you, contrary to your allegations of this morning, referred clearly to the 12th of all? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree, because the page I mentioned, that was on the Internet available, it is page 1668.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the page you're mentioning, sir, relates to the 11th August. As you said --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. The page --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- the page that was read to you by me relates to the 12th. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that you showed me now is to the 12th, yes; and the three pages I mentioned was 1668, page 1670, and page 1671, and these refer to the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree with me, Mr. Hutsch, that I did not read those pages to you, did I?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters kindly ask that pause be maintained between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- I don't know which pages exactly you were presenting me. You were presenting exactly this incident, and this incident took place like not on the 10th. It was taking place in on the 11th. But we are just dancing in a circle. You are putting in some questions out of the content and you're putting in that, and that shows me that we have to continue in German. That's a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, should I proceed in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you can, if you're moving on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'd like to move on to something else. It's the next annotation which you've made in your reporter's notes of the 12th of August of 2001, and I'll bring up the document, once again, so that could you look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P308, please, and I will ask the registry to go to page 9 of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you see a annotation here at 1449 hours. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that it's the last annotation that you made in those notes, and -- well, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I believe that you've told the Office of the Prosecutor that what happened there is that you had reached a check-point, which you say was located at the entrance of the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in experience with the discussion with you, I would not say it was a check-point. It was a police presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you say you saw on that occasion is a scene of beating. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also suggested to the Office of the Prosecutor that a number of individual or members of the MOI had been involved in this matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you claimed also is, that despite what was going on, you managed to bribe your way through this police position, which you called check-points, up to that day, and that you entered the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you said is, in that village, you claim to have recognised a number of individuals, including Mr. Johan Tarculovski, and a person called Goran Stojkov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct that in those notes that you say you took on 12th of August 2001, there is not a word about what you say you saw in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there is not even a word of the fact that you entered that village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the explanation which you gave for that, Mr. Hutsch - and again, correct me if that is not put properly - the suggestion was that you stopped taking notes at the time when you entered the village because that could draw attention on to you and create security issues for you and the people you were with. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the concern that you had is, if the people who were in the village understood who you were and what you were doing, they could get worried and could turn on you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In other words, you didn't want them to know that you were a journalist and visiting the village in that capacity. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What do you mean "no"? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm answering your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you saying that you did not try to hide the fact that you were entering the village in a capacity as a journalist? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what, if anything, then would have prevented the people who were concerned could turn violent on you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Experience shows that if you start to make notices in front of people, or if you start to work with a camera in front of these people, you will be in certain danger, and that is what I tried to avoid. In the moment when you don't show the people that you are making notices or that you are working with a camera, the danger slows down for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that had you entered the village in the manner that you said you did, the people would have known that you were a journalist. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was because you say you had a big press sign stuck to the car, which you say you drove through the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, sir, is that the absence of notice is not because you were afraid of the consequences that could happen to you, but because you never entered the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's not the only abnormal thing about your evidence on that point, and I would like to read to you paragraph which is taken from your statement of August of 2005. That's at paragraph 14. It says this, you the told the Prosecution: "Normally, I do take my notes and drawings directly at the time of the events, or, immediately after." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in that case, Mr. Hutsch, you didn't take any notes after you came out of the village, after 5.30. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, you did; or yes, you didn't?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, you witnessed -- or you witness what you believe to be the scene of very serious crimes, but did not make any record of it, despite the fact that you would have been the only journalist able to enter the village on that day. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know if there had been other journalists as well in side. There must have been journalist inside, at least Macedonian ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that you made many notes, prior to that time, of all sort of incidents, some that could be regarded as important, some as irrelevant, but did you not make a single note of what now say you saw in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's incorrect, because I draw a sketch of one body I saw, or two bodies I saw. What you are trying to say is that Ljuboten, in the afternoon of the 12th, was the big story, and that wasn't. Exactly that's where you over high exactly that -- that theme: If you saw how many journalists were reporting about what was going on in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What putting it to you the reason why there is no note is that you never entered the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your conclusion, again, like all the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- like all the times before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me finish, Mr. Hutsch, please. What I'm putting to you is that the reason you made no notes, either during or after you visited the place, is because you never entered the village and because no one else published information as to what had happened on the 12th up to that point, unlike what happened to the visit of Human Rights watch and OSCE at a later stage; in other words, you did not have information on which to build your story. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect, because like you said, yourself, three years later all this information was available. So what was the problem? The problem was that especially in the Balkans, and especially after the experience in Bosnia and in Kosovo, you deal very carefully with the word "massacre." Like you said, yourself, or like you pointed out from my testimony in the Milosevic trial, until today, I don't know what really happened, for example, in Racak in Kosovo. For that reason, you know exactly, if you go to a scene like that, you have to be very careful with that what you are doing. If there would have been time, if there would have been a importance for the story, I would have tried to investigate the story, but there were no reason for that because, on Monday, we have had the Ohrid Agreement. On Tuesday, we had the discussion in Germany if we would send German soldiers under French command to -- or British command to Macedonia. It was just a story probably for the people in Macedonia but not for the people in Germany, and what are you trying to say here is that this would have been a story for the people in Germany that would have been interesting for them, but that wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Hutsch, that this story, as you call it, made it several international media outlets? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I know that, for example, I think Nick Wood was reporting about that, but then have you to see that possibilities of Nick Wood and the BBC, and you to have to see the possibilities of the Hamburger Adenblatt. We have had, all in all, three pages with politics, and we were one of the leading newspapers who were reporting about the conflict in Kosovo and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, then: Are you saying that entering the village and seeing the scene that you claim you had seen, the commotion that was going on, you had no story; however, you claim that two days later you return to that same village? Were you hoping to get a story two days later, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was thinking that there could be a story, and I tried to convince my editor in chief or head of the political section, Ekbar Nisla [phoen], that he would allow me to investigate that. But after a long discussion that took place on Tuesday - and I think it was intercepted as well this conversation of 45, 50 minutes - we came to the conclusion that the reality is we have the Ohrid Peace Agreement, and German soldiers will be involved in this peace task force. If we bring now a story about Ljuboten and investigate Ljuboten, we have to -- to investigate as well the pressure that was on the Macedonians in Tetovo area where they were forced to leave as well, after the Ohrid Agreement. We had the problem that we had, I think, 11 or 13 missing Macedonians in Tetovo area who were killed by the NLA, and we had several other problems. So we said this story, Ljuboten, isn't leading us to -- to a point that the German people should be informed about. And when I'm informed to write, we were doing just a -- I think we were writing just something from the agency, maybe ten lines, that there have been skirmishes in Ljuboten area, in response of my story from 10th and 11th, where I was doing a story about the mine incident and how this mine incident would be a danger for the peace process. That was before the Ohrid agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is the short answer, Mr. Hutsch, that you published no paper, whether on the 12th or on 14th or after, about the events of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that in your notes, what is you called your reporter's notes of 12th of August 2001, there is not a single reference, for instance, to an encounter with Mr. Tarculovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No reference to any type of gun which you say he was wearing at the time.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And setting aside your little drawing that appears on the 14th of August, is it correct that your notes of 12th contain no reference to any dead bodies in Ljuboten, which you claim to have seen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a sketch with two dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We are going to come to that. Do you agree that the sketch, which you say you did on the 12th, appears on your note of the 14th? Do you agree with that??

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, we'll set them aside and we will come back to them. Is it also correct that, in your notes of the 12th, there is no reference to any of the people that you claim to have seen in the village, including Mr. Goran Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No story about a BTR having driven through a pool of blood. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree -- no, I don't agree, because it is in the sketch, if I'm recalling that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking about your notes at this stage and the time that is relevant after you claim you entered the village. Would you agree that there is nothing that in those notes that would match this. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is no reference to the ammunition, the 9-millimetre ammunition, which five years later you recall seeing on the scene. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to see the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll -- I can show you the sketch, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P320; and in the German one, it would be starting -- it would be page N003-0017.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hutsch, at this stage, I'm asking you about your notes of the 12th. Do you agree that, in those notes of the 12th, there's no reference to any police cars in the village. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, as we mentioned earlier, there is not a reference to any single incident which you've later told to the Office of the Prosecutor and to this Chamber, which you claim to have witnessed in the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's one particular issue or one particular point that I would like now to ask you a few more questions about. You will recall -- I will just ask you a few general questions first. You recall that you've indicated to me today, but also to the Prosecutor earlier in your statement, that on the 12th of August, you saw armoured vehicles, and I believe you mentioned the Hermelin and two BTR-80. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would first like to ask you about the BTR-80, if I may. We will go to the Hermelin in a bit later. Do you recall saying that the BTR, the two BTRs that you said you saw, were mounted with what you believe to be 14.5-millimetre machine-guns. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you remember mentioning that you saw those BTR vehicles on the 10th. Do you recall that? I can turn to your statement if it is of assistance.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay. You remember. Do you recall saying to the Prosecution also that you saw those vehicles on the 11th? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall that you also, here in court but, again, to the Prosecutor in your statement as well, mentioned seeing those vehicles in varies parts of the village in Ljuboten on the 12th of August. Do you recall saying that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will briefly summarise - and, again, correct me if the summary is inaccurate - but in paragraph 64 of the statement, you said that you saw them as part of the so-called "northern attack." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You say you saw these vehicles in the centre of the village, or at least one of those vehicles in the centre of the village. That's paragraph 91. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Also at the entrance of the village, paragraph 107?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you mention the tracks of a BTR in the centre of the village, paragraph 116?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also said that you saw them, at least one of them, at the graveyard, is that correct, paragraph 140?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would mean that you claim to have seen those at least on five occasions during that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I understand, with your military experience, the BTR-80 is a vehicle that would be quite familiar to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not familiar me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that's a vehicle that you knew about. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what I'm putting to you, sir, is that, in fact, you never saw any such vehicles on that day. What I'm putting it to you is that, as with other parts of your stories, you are piecing events and information from different times, different location, different sources, and trying to piece them into your story. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. But probably, probably I'm wrong about what is the BTR, and I should have better said that it was an APC and not to -- to be so precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what you're doing, Mr. Hutsch, is to pull out of a hole, don't you, because the BTR-80, you mention it many, many times in your evidence and in your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, as a military man, would you know what the BTR-80 is, as you acknowledged a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So what, in fact, you call a BTR-80, it varies in parts of your statement. Now you are trying to suggest that it is a different vehicle. Is that what you're doing?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm trying to say that it was an APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll read to you, for instance, what you said in paragraph 64 of your statement: "The northern attack was formed by around 100 police officers. This front was supported by one Hermelin and two BTR-80. You didn't mention any APC or any other category of vehicle, and it goes on to say this: "The Hermelin car was equipped with a light machine-gun fixed with a mount on the APC," and that's referring to the Hermelin. "I think it was a 7.62-millimetre machine-gun. The Hermelin was in grey colour. "The two BTRs -- the two BTR-80 were both equipped with a 14.5 machine-gun -- millimetre machine-gun." And if we look at paragraph 20, for instance, of your statement, it say this, and it talks about Friday, 10th of August: "The leading vehicle was a BTR vehicle followed by one police jeep-type Cherokee," and so on. At paragraph 36 of your statement, it say this and talks about Saturday, the 11th of August: "In Ljubanci, I have seen several positions of the army and the police. On several occasions, the police and army were present at the same time. The scene was a mixture of already prepared positions and temporary presence of units. Some of the units were gathering around APC/BTR-80." So in all cases, and I think there are three or four other reference, Mr. Hutsch, where you specifically stated that this vehicle, this armoured vehicle, is a BTR-80. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, and I have to correct my testimony in this way: I will say it was a APC --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- like I mentioned in my testimony before as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting it to you, sir, is that the Office of the Prosecutor recorded you on five or six occasions, and the transcript of this Tribunal recorded you also making references to a BTR-80, and you never suggested it was anything else. You are now realising that, in fact, those vehicles did not exist at the time in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 1D314, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I will ask you to focus on paragraph 10 of your -- of this statement, please. This is, again, a statement taken by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, and it is taken from a person called Nikoletka Mitanova. And if you look at paragraph 5, it says that, in 2001, this person worked as a assistant of the Minister of the Administration for Finance and Other Common Matters. And at paragraph 7, it says: "In 2001, my tasks included preparing the budget of the MOI, following and controlling of the financial transactions, control of realisation of completed purchases in the sector for material, working and following of the completed investments in the ongoing year." I will ask to you look at paragraph 10, please, where it say this is: "Further more, the police did not have BTR-80 vehicles at its disposal; namely, the Ministry attempted to purchase few such vehicles for the police, but we did not succeed in receiving one during that year. It was either 25th or 26th August that we were finally able to purchase some. I also recall a document which can prove this fact." And then, at paragraph 11, it says: "After the crisis ended in November 2002, machine-gun were mounted on some of them." And before I ask you a question, sir, I'd like to show you another document which is Rule 65 ter 1D316. What will appear in front of you, Mr. Hutsch, is a letter by the Ministry of Interior. It is the Cabinet of the State Secretary, and it is stated the 19th of June of 2007. It's a letter that responds to two particular queries that were made by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, and I will ask to you look at the second part of that document, if I may. It's at the bottom of the page. Thank you. It says: "As a response to item 3 and 4 of your request, and in attempt to provide information as a answer, a telephone conversation was held with Branko Trajanovski, head of the department for training and support in the Department for Special, posebna, Units in the CPS. "We were informed that in 2001 the police have received BTR-80 vehicles for the first time in the end of the month of August; whereas, weapon was mounted on them in 2002." Do you agree that what those documents or the statement and the letter suggests, Mr. Hutsch, is that, in fact, on 10, 11, or 12th of August of 2001, there was no such BTR-80 vehicles in the Ministry of Interior. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what these papers or documents suggest, but have I photos here. One here from March 2001 in Tetovo. I think it is a Reuters picture that shows police forces with a BTR-80. I have another picture in the streets of Tetovo also in March 2001 that shows BTR and police officers, which clearly identify it was a BTR-80. There is another picture that is from August 2001, and it is done by Reuters, I suppose. That shows a BTR-80, and I think it is a T-55, I'm not sure, with police forces on it. Probably, it--

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it is need to be explained --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, we would be very grateful if could you provide those pictures to the parties and give us information as to the dates of those documents and where they were obtained from.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you will find them with Reuters, with AFP, and with EPA, with the news agencies, and they will have the exact date when these pictures was taken. I think both accused will confirm that these pictures are made during the street fightings in -- in spring in Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll look into that, Mr. Hutsch, and now I will turn to the second vehicle, which you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: These documents, are you wanting to tender them or have them marked Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we would be grateful if they could be marked, and we will do an investigation with the Prosecutor, perhaps, that may be necessary in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The three photographs will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D239, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Hutsch, as you mentioned earlier, that you also claim to have seen a Hermelin vehicle with a 7.62-millimetre gun on top of it on the 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I claimed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, there was no such vehicle in the village on that day. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, first, do you agree that the Hermelin which were delivered at the time to Macedonia did not have guns mounted on them. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case, could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D320, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, what will appear in front of you is the statement of the person, who you say became your superior at some stage in September of 2001. It is Mr. Peter Matthiesen who gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like the registry, please, to turn to the fourth page after that document, please, and if we could focus, please, on paragraph 14, please, 1-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I will ask you to look at what is more or less the middle of that paragraph. It starts with the word, "However." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what Mr. Matthiesen says is this: "However, in the time before the armed conflict, Germany delivered material to the army and police such as first aid material, cars, technical equipment, and also armoured carriers such as APCs known as Hermelins. The aid was always delivered on the restrictions to avoid that the material could be used against the civilian population in Macedonia.". Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he says: "For example, the Hermelins were delivered without any mount for machine-guns on top of the APC." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what Mr. Matthiesen suggests is, in fact, the Hermelin that were given, at least as far as Germany is concerned, to the Macedonian authority were given without this machine-gun mounted on top of it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without German machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what they said is that there was no mounts on the Hermelin which they gave or sold to the Macedonian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of any other countries that sold or gave Hermelins to the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to prove that I am saying the truth here, we have another picture, I think it is Reuters as well, that shows Hermelins with what I think is the Russian machine-gun 7.62-millimetres that was put up to the Hermelin by the Macedonian security forces.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that you are not right. When I am right, this photo was taken in the area of Ljuboten, and that means north going to Tanusevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what is correct, Mr. Hutsch, is that guns mounted Hermelin were mounted on the Hermelin after the events to which you refer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you do here, again, is as you did with many other aspects of your evidence, is to piece different aspects of things seen in one part of the country events known from a different time and try to fit them into your story. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that are you doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me show you Rule 65 ter 1D314. This is the same statement, Mr. Hutsch, of Nikoletka Mitanova, which I read to you a moment ago. I will ask you this time to look at paragraph 8 and 9, and it says this: "During the 2001 crisis, the police had Hermelin vehicles at its disposal. Some of them were purchased from Germany. During the 2001 crisis period, not a single Hermelin had machine gun mounted on it. They were used for transport of the police forces in the area where the risk of attacks were significantly higher." I'll now ask to you turn to what is Rule 65 ter 1D316. It is again this letter, Mr. Hutsch, that I have shown you a moment ago. I will draw your attention to, this time, the first section of that letter, and it say this is. This is, again, the letter of the State Secretary, Mr. Goce Duklevski [phoen], to the team of Mr. Boskoski, and it says: "For items 1 and two of your request, we inform you that the Ministry of Interior Affairs has dispatched information to the Minister of Defence, with the Act," and then there is a number, "where among else it is stated that, quote/unquote, 'During the armed conflict in the Republic of Macedonia 2001, all the members of the police used armoured vehicles Hermelin, but only for the purpose of transportation of persons due to the facts that there were not fixated weapons on this armoured vehicle.'" Would you agree that what this suggests - the letter is not very helpful, I agree - but do you agree that the statement of Ms. Mitanova is that, in fact, during the crisis period - and that would be until the 13th of August, one would think - the Hermelin were not, or the Hermelin of the police in any case, were not mounted with machine-guns. Do you agree that's what the statement suggests?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We should marked for identification the fourth photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D240, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, sir, you were doing semantics here. The reality, from the evidence of Mr. M-037, is that there was no gun. What are you trying to suggest now is a play of word about the concept of mounting. What I'm putting to you that there was no gun, whether mounted or otherwise, placed on the top of the Hermelin in the village. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that because that is exactly not what Mr. M-037 said. Mr. M-037 said that there was no mounted machine on gun on the top, that there was just installations. But what I say is there was a machine-gun there. If it was mounted, okay. I'm not precise in this point, and we are doing exactly the semantic discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, not only are you claiming to have seen things, Mr. Hutsch, that could you not possibly have seen at the time, but what you do also is that you place things in the wrong places. I'm going to give you a example.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown exhibit P296, please. This does not appear to be P296.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think this is a protected witness, is it, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. That is not the document in question, Your Honour, that we're asking for. So we'll skip this one for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It hasn't been published outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, and we will come back to it when we have located the exact reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall saying on the 21st of June of 2007 in this courtroom - it is at page 2525 to 2527 - that you recall a command and logistic centre of the army that was placed at the children's rest house which is close to the Saint Nikola monastery. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you say what's the basis of that knowledge of yours? Is that a visit or is that information which you obtained from other people?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly, I got this information from other people; partly, I saw vehicles, logistical vehicles, going into this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If, if I remember right, it was not possible for to us enter exactly this area because there was a barrier and a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So are you not claiming, Mr. Hutsch, that you actually went into that location. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then I'd like to ask you to see another document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be -- well, we can return to the previous point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Apparently, it has been located now, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that would be exhibit P296, and I'm grateful to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Hutsch, that this is one of the drawings which you made on the 27th of August of 2005 and which you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall making a number of annotations of what you said were MUP gathering assembly areas, I think you called it, and other logistic centres which we just discussed right now. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you explain when or on what basis, rather, you prepared that particular drawing?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly, from what I saw myself; partly, from things that we were told or I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So could you indicate, for example, what you say you saw yourself. For example, I think I count four MUP assembly areas. Is that -- are those things which you say you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we've seen already about the logistic centre. You've indicated that you actually didn't visit the site. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what about the school which you've indicated there?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was passing once the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what about the football field where you located the MUP assembly area?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I saw as well, that there was a crowd of police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay. Next to the football field; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Next to the football field?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, he'd like to read out to you a passage from the evidence of another witness who has testified in this case. It is Mr. Mitre Despodov who testified here on the 26th of June 2007, and it is at page 2672. I will go on for a couple of pages. It starts like this, and the question is: "In the village of Ljubanci, there was a police check-point by a house of Brace the so-called Chinese wall?" The answer is: "This is how people call it, but the precise location is across the nearby the football playing field. "Is that correct that right at the football place, the playground, there was a police check-point?" "Yes, that's correct. This is a crossroad that goes to the village of Ljuboten and towards the children's holiday resort." Then the question: "Is it correct that the football playing field is away from the school where your post was, around three to 400 metres?" "Yes, more or less." "This means that the football playing ground is not across the school. Is that correct?" "No." And then the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski asked the witness to be shown the document, which I wrongly numbered as P296, which was in fact D296, which led to the -- it is the same picture, but with our number. And then, if you go to page 2674 of this same witness, he is being asked that: "According to your statement, this is a sketch which is incorrect, since the football field is located at another position, another place. Is this correct?" "Yes." "This means that the person who drew the sketch, prepared this sketch, does not correspond with the sketch of the village." "Yes." "Can you observe on this sketch, in the middle above the football feed, you can see a cross with a circle beneath it?" "Yes." "If this is the location on the command of the 2nd Infantry Company, I'm sure that it won't be correct that say that members of Ministry of Interior are located on the positions marked with the lettering 'MUP.' You can see three different positions indicated." "Yes." "This means that this information on this sketch, according to your opinion, is incorrect?" "No." "Very well. Thank you. This means that this sketch is inaccurate." "Yes, it is inaccurate." This was the evidence Mr. Despodov. I'd like to read out to you another part of the record of the proceedings, and this time this is the evidence of a person called Mario Jurisic who testified on the 6th of July of 2007. And he was asked, again, by counsel for Mr. Tarculovski, he was asked this: "In the village of Ljubanci, there is a football stadium or football playing field. Do you know about that?" "Yes." "Is it correct that it is quite a distance from the school where the command was stationed?" "Yes." And then the counsel asked: "Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P296." And the question is: "Towards the middle of the sketch, can you see a place marked with 'school,' in English." "Yes, I see it." And the question is: "Can you see that next to it, from the left hand side of it, there is the football field as it is written." "Yes." "Is it correct that there is no football field there at that location? It is not where the football field in the village of Ljubanci is located?" And he says: "I have a problem with the orientation on this map. So there is further exchange, and then at the next page, it is page 3370, is the following exchange: "Could you explain to us where is the football field actually located? Where on this map would it actually be located, in your opinion, from the school?" "It should be right from the school." "Thank you. Could I ask for the assistance of the usher to help the witness to use the stylus and mark the location of the football field." And the witness said: "Roughly here. I can't be more precisely because this is a sketch, but it would be somewhere here." And then the document, which has been marked by Mr. Jurisic, was admitted as 2D28.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like the registry to bring up Exhibit 2D28.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you can see, Mr. Hutsch, this is the same drawing as was shown to you before with one difference, and it is a red square marked by the witness Mr. Jurisic. As can you see, Mr. Jurisic placed the football pitch, not where you say you saw it with a gathering of MUP persons, but on the other side, towards the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's something which you told me earlier you had observed yourself, is that correct, the location of the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I observed police forces in the area of the football field, and that's what I think it was by the first witness confirmed. Probably, three years, four years after the incident, I don't remember exactly where the football field might have been. Yeah. That might be my mistake on this points, but I don't understand what we are discussing about now: Where is the football field in Ljubanci, or if there have been police forces in Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the relevance of this, Mr. Hutsch, is, as you said, not necessarily the real location of the football pitch, but the fact that you are unable to place particular matters which you claim to have seen with your own eyes and are ready to make drawings and present to this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another one I would like to show, and it is exhibit P317.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Hutsch, this was a picture that was shown to you by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The transcript is at 2748 to 2749, and you made a number of annotations on this document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall, in particular at page 2748 and following, you made a particular annotation as to a place where you said there was a check-point. Do you recall making that annotation with the word "CP"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is what you see with the number 2 in your drawing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness now please be shown what is Exhibit 223, please; exhibit P223, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have the picture in front of you, Mr. Hutsch? That should be the same view, if you wish, with a different marking. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this picture was shown to a villager, Mr. Mahmuti Ismaili, who testified before this Trial Chamber. He was shown, as you can see, the same picture as was shown of you, and he was asked a number of questions about this particular matter. I would like to read to you the passage in question. It is the 23rd of May of 2007, and it's at page 1345 through 1346. It starts with a request by the Prosecution that a picture be shown. It is 19921 which is this picture without the marking. The witness is asked this: "What do you recognise on this picture?" "On this picture there was the police check-point." And it says: "Where was the police check-point, please?" "Here. The main police check-point was here." And the question was: "Can you please encircle where you believe that the check-point was." And he says: "The check-point was a little bit closer, but you can't see it here, and here it was where they made us lie down on the ground. The women were separated from the men. You can't see the check-point here." And then a further question by the Prosecutor: "Witness, you just said that you can't see the check-point, but you also said you were -- you can't see it in the picture." And then the question is: "You also said that there was a location where you were asked to lay down. Can you encircle that place, please." And that is the circle that Mr. Ismaili made.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Kindly slow down a little bit Mr. Mettraux, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, he is being asked: "Do you know the name of this place? And he says: "Kodra e Zajmit." "Is there another name for Kodra e Zajmit?" "I don't know. This is the part of my field, my father's field, and we called it "Kodra e Zajmit" meaning "Zajmit's field." "Where is the places where you have been beaten?" And he says: "Here, the place that I encircled." Then, it was received as a exhibit, P223. Do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, when the Mr. Ismaili was asked whether there was a check-point that visible anywhere on this picture, he said that there wasn't. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux. We are again in a semantic discussion; and before I answer, I would like to see how I was defining all these circles and lines I was doing there. Because if I see that right, a small circle that this witness made, it's around 50 metres in the circle. And what I say is, in this complete time, there were much more space where the things took place; and, definitely, this witness said at this point when have been -- women have been separated from men, and that happened exactly in this area. So in the moment, I can't see the widespread, and we have had the problem. If there's a check-point, if there is a police presence, if there's a control post, whatever, we have had that for the last two days or this day and the last day of my further testimony, and it is a semantic discussion again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, what I'm putting to that you is that you claim to have seen something that someone from the village did not see on that very same location. What I'm putting it to you is that whereas Mr. Ismail was being truthful about this matter, you weren't. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We are talking about a check-point, and there was. That's what I said in my experience in the discussion with you. It might be a police presence, and that is exactly the problem. This witness could testify in his mother tongue and not me, and we are now in a conflict for the right words in English. That is neither mine nor your more tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, don't you think there would be something awkward, to put it that way, that, as you suggest, a jeep vehicle with press markings on it should be stopped at what you claim was a check-point there, and that no one from the village claimed to have seen that vehicle. Would you agree that this would be awkward?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something I can't imagine because villagers would have seen us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the point, Mr. Hutsch. The strange thing about it is that the villagers did not suggest that they had seen you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I'm wondering that, on the other side, you are on a delay with all the witnesses. On the other side, you had the possibility to have the testimony of all villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to put it differently --?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a little bit astonishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am going to put it differently to you, Mr. Hutsch. I am going to put it those terms. Do you agree that not a single villager from Ljuboten on the 12th of August of 2001 could possibly have seen you in the village, since you did not enter the village? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it is your conclusion that you buy or that you sell as a reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason why not a single villager could have seen you where you say there was a check-point on that particular location is because you were not there. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that you should tell me what is in your eyes a check-point, and then we will find if I would say that the check-point or police presence or whatever else. We are in a circle again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think, Mr. Hutsch, there's more than a problem of circle here, and I'd like to show what you is exhibit P19, please. Thank you. Mr. Hutsch, do you recall being shown this picture of Mr. Sulejman Bajrami --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- by the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you recall that you were asked by the Office of the Prosecutor to make a number markings on this picture? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown what is Exhibit P319, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise the drawing Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, correct me if my summary of what I say is incorrect, but I understand you to have been saying that the red drawn up body on the top of the picture was actually the same body as we see on the picture that you said it had been moved slightly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you told the Chamber is that at number 2, where the feet of what you say, was the body of another person lying down at the time here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you say is number 3 was the casings or casing residue from weapons that had been used. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the distance between the bodies and the casings you estimated at between three and ten metres. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The number 4, you said, refers to what you say you had identified as a bullet casing. That is correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, I believe you also said that you had been told that the second body, which would be on the second picture, was that of Muharem Bajrami. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful with that. You see there is a problem with this particular assertion of yours that there were two bodies in this place. What I'm putting to you, in fact, Mr. Hutsch, is that your belief was that the blood, which appears or which can be seen on the picture, was the blood of another person; whereas, in fact, it is the blood of the body of the person Sulejman Bajrami that has been pushed to the side. What I am putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that there never was a second body and that you have invented it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. That's what you see here as well. Under the body, there is no -- no evidence for any blood. So it was clear that this body was moved and that this bloody -- that the blood, I didn't say that was belonging to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that there was never a second body to be seen on this picture, contrary to what have you claimed. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I am putting to you is that you realised, at some stage during the preparation of your evidence, that there was a problem with that, with this picture. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the problem is this, Mr. Hutsch: You have referred to a little drawing several times that you made, you say, in your notes of the 14th of August; but in this courtroom, you have claimed for the first time, or to be more precise for the second time since you mentioned it in the proofing, that, in fact, you had done the drawing on the 12th, although in the record it's of the 14th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason why there was a problem, and you realised that there was a problem, Mr. Hutsch, is this. You were shown by the Prosecutor pictures of this particular body taken on the 14th of August, and there was not two but one body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect, because the first time I saw this photo was when we prepared my testimony here one day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you realise that you could not claim that there were two bodies on the 14th of August, when there was photographic record from that date showing clearly that there was in fact only one body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you did is to then claim that, in fact, you had prepared this little drawing, which I will show to you in a minute, and said: "Although it appears in the notes of the 14th, I did it on the 12th when I saw these two bodies." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that this is another one of your fabricated stories. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that in the two lengthy statements that you mentioned -- that you had - I'm sorry - with the Office of the Prosecutor, the only place where you mentioned the body of Mr. Sulejman Bajrami, which we can see on in picture, is in relation to the 14th of August of 2001. That's when you claim to have seen him. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that you didn't mention the body of Mr. Sulejman Bajrami in your notes of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was. I was drawing him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that the only place where he appears in your statement and in your notes, these reporter's notes, is on the 14th, do you agree with that, not on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me show you your statement. At page 8 of your statement, it would be again Rule 65 ter 1D234. At paragraph 51, you start recounting the events of Sunday, 12 August of 2001. Your discussion of this particular day, the 12th of August of 2001, goes up to paragraph 148, where you say: "On Sunday 12 August 2001, there was no official comment of the Ministry of Interior about the police operation in Ljuboten, and there was no comment in reference to the killed persons. The only official information was the television footage and comment broadcasted on the same evening."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the registry, please, to bring up page 21 of the statement. That will be 1D00-2587.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at paragraph 148, that's the paragraph I just read to you, and then it goes on at paragraph 149 saying: "Only two days later, on Tuesday, 14 August 2005 [sic], late afternoon, it was confirmed that there were persons killed in Ljuboten, but that they were for sure terrorists." It goes on in this paragraph. And at paragraph 150, you are saying this: "It was the same day when I was visiting Ljuboten the second time with a lot of my journalist colleagues. For this day, I kept another reporter's notebook. I attach a copy of this notebook to my statement." And then this in paragraph 151: "The most significant events on these days, I can summarize in following subjects: The corpses of the killed bodies were still in the village. At the least the body Murahem Bajrami, 65 years, full name are identified, was moved from his original position.
