Being asked, I mean the body of the older man which was lying beneath Sulejman Bajrami. This was the name which was told to me." It also mentioned that: "I also visited the crime scene where Rami Jusufi was killed. I spoke with his father Elmaz Jusufi." Do you agree that, as far as your statement is concerned, Mr, Hutsch, those comments about the two bodies are made in the part of your section that deal with your alleged visit on the 14th. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were going to -- no. I don't understand this question in this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can rephrase it again. Is that correct that you only refer in your statement to the body of Sulejman Bajrami and having seen them, and the moving that you say went on the description in paragraph 151 which I just tried, in that section of your statement which relates to the 14th of August? Perhaps, I can shorten the question and make it simpler for you because it wasn't very clear. Do you agree that the description which you give of the two bodies next to each other and the fact that one had been moved is made in the context of what you say was your second visit on the 14th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That this older man, he was taken away from this place. If I have the scene right in my mind, the street is -- it's going a little bit down; and, on other side, there is the entrance of a house. On this Tuesday, if you were opening the door, left hand, the older man was lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the short answer to my question was: Yes, you made those comments in the context of 14th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can look at your reporter's notes, once again, of this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is exhibit P320, please, and I would like the registry to show to Mr. Hutsch page N003-0017.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, that's the drawing. Do you recognise the drawing that you made --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- of what you said you saw, Mr. Hutsch? At this stage, do you agree that this drawing was made in your notes, reporter's notes, not of the 12th but of the 14th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that it does not appear in the notes which you have dated the 14th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I think I was telling here, to the Chamber as well, that I was doing this sketch on the evening of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's what you said, Mr. Hutsch, but you never said it before you came to The Hague. What I'm telling to you, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that you made up that story, which contradicts both this reporter's notes and your own statement because it had become impossible for to you suggest that you could have seen those two bodies on the 14th next to each other. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what I am putting to you further, Mr. Hutsch, is not only was it impossible for to you see that on the 14th, but could you not even see it on the 12th. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what I am putting to you, so that it is clear, Mr. Hutsch, I'm putting it to that you lied about this. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you a something else again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could bring up what is Exhibit P19 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Hutsch, that that is the same -- do you recognise that is the same picture that I showed you a moment ago? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, this picture, Mr. Hutsch, was shown to another person, another witness in this case, and this person is Mr. Isni Ali, who testified in this case on the 13th of July of 2007. This would be at page 3494, 3459, and it goes on to 3496 where the document is admitted. I would like to read out to you what this person, Mr. Isni Ali, told this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As we do so, I'll ask the registry to bring up Exhibit 2D32, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is in response to questions by my colleague, Mr. Apostolski, on the 13th of July of 2007, and Mr. Apostolski asked first: "Could the witness please be shown the exhibit P19." That's the picture you still have in front of you. He was asking this of the witness: "Can you tell me, can you recognise Sulejman Bajrami in this picture, in this photograph?" "No. He was killed here on this place, on this spot." "Can you tell me at what time you passed by his body on Sunday." "At about 6.00, we went there above and I saw -- I saw him from the other side." "When we're speaking -- we are speaking about 6.00 in the afternoon?" "Yes, in the afternoon, at about 6.00. I don't know the exact time." Mr. Ali was talking about the 12th of August, Mr. Hutsch. The question of Mr. Apostolski is this: "Was his body at this location where you were passing by." "No. He was closer to the street." Then Mr. Apostolski says: "Could I ask for the assistance of the usher to help the witness mark the location where we are seeing the body of Sulejman Bajrami." Question: "If you could circle that in the photograph, the location where the body of Sulejman Bajrami was lying." The witness did so. "Could you please use a arrow to show where his feet were facing? Would this circle be his head?" "This way," the witness said, "and I didn't really have time to see where was foot or where were his fingers. I didn't get very close to see where he -- where was exactly his finger. My family was behind me." And then further down the page, well, His Honour Judge Parker said: "Could I just note for the record that number 1 depicts the head and number 2 the feet." Then Mr. Apostolski asked a further question, and he says: "Did you see any other body, apart from the body of Sulejman Bajrami, immediately next to his?" "No, no. There was no other body." "So, if anyone else were to state before this Court that next to the body of Sulejman Bajrami there was another body, it would not be correct?" And he says: "A little further, to the door of Sabri Ahmeti, was lying the body of Muharem," he called it, "Muharem Bajrami, 20 to 30 metres further; and, here, next to Sulejman Bajrami, there was no one. He was alone." What I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that this story that you made up is completely false, and that you never saw this scene from inside the village. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I would like to see first what I was drawing, and I will see that exactly my drawing and the drawing of this witness is quite similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, you see, Mr. Hutsch --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me finish, please. Second, if I recall right, the older body, I was doing an arrow that he was laying a little bit out of the window of the picture. Probably, we have to check that with the transcript that I said that he was a little bit out of the -- of the picture. And I was doing, and that's what I saw a few minutes before, that I was doing a arrow that he was in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, what you're doing is you're misleading the Court. That's what you're doing. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm saying all the time from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm putting to is what Mr. Isni Ali was the truth, which is the body that you see on this picture was before the 14th, or at some stage between the 12th and 14th when it was placed on the side of the road where it is now, at the time on the 12th of August, it was only in the middle of the road where Mr. Isni drew it and where the blood is. There was no other body. As Mr. Isni pointed out, the body which claim was there was, in fact, 20 or 30 metres away from that scene. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that it was 20 or 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that, once again, you fabricated this story from the material which you got from Human Rights Watch. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall you were wondering how someone could have drawn or could have made up the little drawing that you say you did first on the 14th, then on the 12th, without having been in the village? Do you recall asking me that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think I can assist you here, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to show Rule 65 ter 1D348.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is the Internet version of the report of Human Right Watch concerning -- the title is "Crimes Against Civilian Abuses by Macedonian forces in Ljuboten, August 10 to 12, 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look just under the title, there's a reference to "photo gallery." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you click on that photo gallery, Mr. Hutsch, you would reach that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That is the next page of that document, please, and if we could enlarge perhaps the centre of the pictures, please, the middle pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise for the definition on the picture, Mr. Hutsch, this is not of great quality, but if could you look at the picture in the middle. You will see on the picture which says "46K" that's the picture or a slightly different shot of the same picture that was P19. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible for me to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page, please, and that would be if you click on the picture marked 46k. And if the registry could go a little bit lower in this picture, please, a little bit down. Thank you. And a little bit to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: See, that's the picture of Mr. Sulejman Bajrami which was freely available on the Internet on the Human Rights web site, and it shows the body of Mr. Bajrami. This is not the same picture as you were shown. There are one or two details which are different, but it is the same location, and the pool of blood is there. What I am putting to you, sir, is that your little drawing, that you made in your note of the 14th, you based it on this picture. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, because in my drawing there is a second dead body.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was your mistake, wasn't it, that you claim there was a second body there, where in fact there was no one. The body which had been in this pool of blood was the same one as we see on the picture, as Mr. Ali said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't that correct, Mr. Hutsch, that you have indicated earlier that you didn't publish a piece on the 12th because there was low interest on the part of your editorial. Is that correct? Do you recall saying that, that you couldn't convince your editor.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that, when asked by me about why you didn't write the story on the 14th, you said that you had been given a different assignment in Tetovo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's a different assignment?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That you said you had been asked or requested to cover another story for your newspaper. Is this correct? Do you want me to rephrase it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct that the story should be another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that, when you testified in the Milosevic case, you testified that you had been to Racak at the time when there was activity about the "massacre"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were also asked, during the Milosevic proceedings, why you did not publish an article about this story. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will help you perhaps, but perhaps can you recall why you didn't write the piece at the time.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same because it became unclear for me what was really going on. And to investigate, to research a thing like that is very expensive, it is very expensive, it costs time. It is for a journalist doing that in a serious way nearly impossible to finish that within two days, three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, your answer at the time -- the question that was put to you, and this is Prosecutor from Milosevic. It is IT-02-54-T. The date is 12th of October 2004. The page is 32935. The question that was asked of you was this: "Having considered the scene at the ravine, where else did you go after that if you take us further on your route through Racak from that moment?" And then there is your answer. You were examined by Mr. Kaye: It was about 2.00, 1400 hours, that I left the scene of the crime, went down to the town, and left for Pristina. Basically, this was because I was given a different assignment by my own paper, but the other reason was I wanted to finish my report." So, once again, Mr. Hutsch, you had claimed to have been to a significant incident in the conflict in the Balkans. And when asked why you didn't publish the piece about this matter, your answer was: "Well, I was given a different assignment by my own paper." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he never published any paper about Racak either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but probably you would tell the Chamber for what newspaper I was working in this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I don't think this is very relevant at this stage, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you feel you have mention this paper, you should be free to do it.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a weekly, Stern; and exactly for a weekly, there is nobody interested in actual news, like in a daily. They are just interested in background stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And by contrast, a daily would be interested in that sort of story. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the Hamburger Adenblatt is a daily. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We were planning to go for five or ten more minutes, Mr. Mettraux, but if you have run out the steam.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly not. We can continue for as long as you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems that there is a view that probably the cross-examination would be more efficient if it was continued tomorrow, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be refreshed in any case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. So that we might then adjourn now and we do so for the reasons that you raised yesterday, and we continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.59 p.m.,
